MI-senate.statusNote: Open seat: Abdul El-Sayed (D) won the Aug 4 primary over Haley Stevens; Mike Rogers (R) is the Republican nominee.

candidates.name: Abdul El-Sayed
candidates.background: Physician and epidemiologist; former Detroit health director and Wayne County health official; author of 'Medicare for All: A Citizen's Guide.' Won the August 2026 Democratic primary.

cost.label: Union member (SEIU/AFT/UAW); campaigns on expanding union protections and worker power (Wikipedia)

health.label: Supports Medicare for All; co-wrote a book on it (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Backed repealing state preemption of rent control (2018) (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Supports abolishing ICE while keeping 'certain kinds' of border enforcement (Wikipedia)

climate.label: 100% renewable energy by 2030; tougher environmental enforcement (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Mike Rogers
candidates.background: Former FBI special agent and U.S. Representative (2001–2015), chaired the House Intelligence Committee; 2024 Senate nominee, running again in 2026.

cost.label: Argues controlling federal spending and rates — not intervention — lowers costs (Wikipedia)

health.label: Voted repeatedly against Medicare drug-price negotiation; opposes ACA provisions, favors free-market care (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Backs border wall and stricter enforcement; blames 'open borders' for crime (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Emphasizes cutting federal spending; backs Trump tariff plans (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Former FBI agent (organized crime); campaigns on tougher enforcement (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Says he won't try to overturn Michigan's 2022 abortion-rights amendment; leaves issue to states (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Backs aggressive election-security measures incl. police monitoring of election workers; promoted 2020 fraud claims (Wikipedia)
